subject: HelioCorp POC — data readout and next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heliocorp.com>, Natalie Park <natalie.park@heliocorp.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: HelioCorp POC — data readout and next steps

Hi Liam / Natalie —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan for the trial: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: reduce customer support triage time by surfacing the correct KB article and suggested next actions from inbound tickets.
- Success criteria you mentioned: 70%+ top-1 accuracy on KB retrieval, median inference latency < 250ms for single-request path, and economic goal of <$8 per 1k inference tokens during sustained traffic.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks sandbox + 4-week trial)
- Phase 0 (this week): prompt/log sample transfer, data whitelist, and security review.
- Phase 1 (sandbox): Redwood ingests prompts/logs, we run baseline runs and sync on initial metrics (3 business days).
- Phase 2 (trial): 4-week volume run with agreed routing/latency SLOs and weekly checkpoints.

What we need from your side to kick off
1) A sample of ~1k real prompts/log lines (anonymized) + a small labeled set (~200 rows) where you’ve mapped to the correct KB article or action — CSV is fine.
2) Indicate the internal owner for data delivery and any network constraints (S3 bucket, secure Share, or Drive link).
3) Any non-standard security requirements or data fields we should scrub before ingestion.

Attachments: none from us right now — we can send a short SOW + transfer instructions once we confirm the delivery mechanism.

Can you confirm who will be responsible for exporting the logs and whether S3 presigned URL works for you? If that works, we’ll share an encrypted bucket and a checklist for PII redaction.

Tentative kickoff: if we get data by EOD Wed (11/11) we can start Phase 0 on Thu 11/12.

Thanks —
Dylan

-- 
Dylan Brooks

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming: S3 presigned URL is fine — our platform team will upload. I’m looping in Natalie (product ops) as the internal owner for the export and delivery.

Per your request I attached a small sample and an index of the fields we can export. The sample is anonymized; it contains 1,050 prompt rows and 220 labeled mappings to KB article IDs (labels in column kb_id).

Attachments: [Attachment: prompt_sample_list.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

Two quick notes/questions:
- Can Redwood accept UTF-8 CSV with columns: request_id, user_message, timestamp, kb_id (optional), context_blob (optional)?
- For the labeled subset, we have subjective label quality — is your eval tolerant of some label noise, or do you prefer that we supply a smaller, higher-precision set?

We’ll plan to upload to a presigned S3 link. Natalie — can you confirm ETA and whether we should encrypt before upload?

—Liam

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelioCorp POC — data readout and next steps

Thanks Liam — this looks perfect for Phase 0. A few clarifications on Redwood’s eval plan and acceptance criteria so we’re aligned before ingestion: 

Eval plan (what we’ll compute)
- Data validation pass (schema, UTF-8, delivery completeness).
- Baseline retrieval accuracy: compute top-1 and top-3 accuracy against your kb_id labels for the labeled 220 rows.
- Latency profile: p50, p95, p99 for single-request synchronous path under synthetic concurrency (to approximate real traffic).
- Regression checks: compare sandbox model outputs to baseline heuristics where available.

Acceptance thresholds you can sign off on (suggested)
- Top-1 accuracy >= 70% on labeled sample.
- Top-3 accuracy >= 85% on labeled sample.
- Median end-to-end latency (decode + routing) < 250ms p50; p95 < 600ms (for your expected payload sizes).
- No severe safety flags on >= 99% of responses (we’ll run our safety heuristics).

Data handling & transfer
- S3 presigned is fine. Please upload to the presigned bucket we’ll send shortly. Encrypt in transit (HTTPS); server-side encryption on upload is optional if you prefer client-side encryption.
- Please remove or hash any direct PII columns (full name, email) — we can assist with a redaction checklist.

Owners and timeline
- HelioCorp data owner: Natalie Park (product ops) — Natalie to upload by EOD Thu 11/12.
- Redwood ingestion & baseline runs: Ava Chen (engineering lead) and Marissa Cole (evaluation) — runs start Fri 11/13, initial results by Mon 11/16.
- Trial kickoff (if results align): week of 11/16 — we’ll propose a 30-minute checkpoint on Mon 11/16 or Tue 11/17.

Attachments: we’ve attached our draft short SOW and a transfer checklist for your legal/security review.
Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-poc-sow-v1.pdf (PDF, 22KB)]

If Natalie can confirm upload ETA and whether you want us to provide a small redaction script, we’ll queue the ingestion pipeline.

Thanks —
Ava
